DISCLAIMER: I'm not a Voat or Reddit admin, I'm just a user who recently (like, an hour ago) joined Voat after moving from Reddit.

I'm curious to know your opinions. Do you want Voat to be Reddit-but-without-censorship? Do you want it to be something completely new? What are you wanting Voat to be?
What do you want to see in a site like Voat?

I want it to be free, basically. Uncensored discussion, cultivating a culture where people aren't afraid to speak their opinions, no matter if others find them enlightening, repugnant, or ridiculous. Everything else beyond that is just a bonus.
I agree. I would love the community to expand more. here is hoping this article brings a couple more users our way: http://www.bbc.com/news/technology-32749408
A healthy community culture... Less 'circle jerking' and more acceptance for differing opinions. More support for OC vs disproportional support for the easy lols (memes, etc.).

I think that, as it is new, that is on US to uphold. We need to set a culture early of people posting content without attributing sources (More importantly people claiming to have made something they didn;t)

oh yes, that as well. when the whole 'source' culture started I loved it. Although I recall in english class it was annoying as hell cause my teachers essentially assumed you yourself could not have your own ideas and you needed to only cite others ideas (my teachers were assholes) but now its all about using sources to give weight to your points or to give credit where its due.
I was moreso referring to posting content and calling out BS when someone claims it's theirs. We need the culture to pick that upnow, not later.
Circle jerking is cathartic. I think the only way to prevent it consuming an entire community is through actively discouraging it.

It is... its so nice to feel like your thoughts and ideas are validated by the masses. but the knee jerk group think reactions are terrible. I dont think we can discourage circle jerking so much as encourage critical thinking.

Why wouldn't we be able to discourage it? I'm not thinking anything draconian, just more of a "flag -> circlejerking"

This wouldn't remove the post, or be negative in any way, except that other users would be able to see if a post was heavily flagged (maybe if there were more flags than up/down votes for a single post) and go "Hey, maybe this isn't great behavior."

I love circle jerking, to be honest. Validation is great. But it eventually disrupts the signal/noise ratio.

Honestly I do love the idea of flagging in general to convey a better opinion of a post. So that people can express something other than 'liking' that your dad died from a heart attack, those awkward limited communication situations.

Imgur has tagging, something like that system could be used but I think giving the tags or flags a numerical weight helps too.

IMO circlejerking, low-quality content and reposting can all be traced back in the most part to fake internet points and ego-stroking. This site might easily go the way of reddit if the same system is used.
Very true, I guess there are two reasons then for circle jerking - validation and gamification. I had considered the first but not the second.

So you suggest removing the 'karma' points? Honestly, I like that. I feel like so many pointless comments are made in an attempt to get karma rather than because they add to the conversation. What others things could substitute karma and avoid the undesirable side effects?

Either remove completely or at least make it so that the points are tied to the individual submissions rather than the user, so you wouldn't be able to "stack" karma points.

I don't know what could be a good alternative, but some people's suggestions of making the score invisible might already help reduce the abuse: often people on reddit downvote simply because they see a negative score so they already get in the mindset of "Yeah this comment is bad", and the same applies in the opposite case I think.

I think, above all else, I want Voat to be a site for free speech. I liked Reddit, I mean hell that's why I used it for so long. But I always felt like they could be more transparent. Everytime they've pulled some shady shit I've gotten closer to making the move permanent, and those instances are becoming more and more common.

Every other month a vote on the default subverse's so ones that fall out of favour may be removed quickly. (See the athiesm subreddit was a default for too long)

this would need some caveats:

1: Sub mods would have to be asked to join the poll, not the other way around

2: Every six months make sure the system is working so it can scale

3: a quick and easy way to add/remove all default subs to your subscriptions.

A real monetization strategy that is in line with user's desires and doesn't rely on ads. I am not against ads, but they are not congruous with the best user experience and they tend to support censorship.

Also, the site should be a 501c with user ownership.

Honestly? A friendlier community, one where average users matter a little more and corporate users, power users, and site politics matter less. Maybe that just means a smaller community, but ideally it'd be able to scale.

Not that I have any idea how to do that, but I'm hopeful about a couple things Voat's doing. Comment score requirements to vote, especially to downvote, should really help cut down on brigading and make bans more meaningful. Showing up and downvotes on every post is nice. I like that Voat seems to be into letting the community grow organically and only policing content for illegality. So maybe there's hope! Or maybe Eternal September is going to chase us down like Anton Chigurch, no matter where we go. Who knows!
I want one vote to count as one vote.
Equality and freedom of ideas. People can say anything they want, I don't want them banned even if it's something I heartily disagree with.
A cerebral user interface that I can plug directly into my brain and bypass my feeble fingers and pathetically slow eye balls.

I'd love to see Voat have a bit more of an intelligent bent. Maybe be a place where people can come together and actually employ a bit of critical thinking and not succumb to the lowest common denominator. There are a few subverses I've seen that encourage intelligent debate, and it gives me hope. Hope that maybe this community can work.

• No haste to be the first to post some kind of reference or meme for the karma points.
  • Useful conversation that doesn't degrade into childish insults (that's hard to avoid on any website, sadly).
  • Emphasis on fascinating and thought-provoking content instead of easy-to-digest memes and image macros.
  • More power in the users' hands and less in the mods' hands.
